title: A shop's Net term reaches QuickBooks as a standard term on first use
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the test organization is connected to a QuickBooks Online sandbox company, and you can sign in to that company in another tab.
  • Make sure the shop's own term A (made for this test), due 14 days after the invoice date, is not in QuickBooks' Terms list.
  • Make sure work order 1 (made for this test) is complete, for a customer who holds term A.
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. On work order 1's Finance tab, set Invoice Date to Oct 5, 2026.
  2. Click Create Invoice.
  3. Wait until the invoice has synced to QuickBooks (it is no longer on the QB Unexported report).
  4. In QuickBooks, open the Terms list (Settings, All lists, Terms).
  5. In QuickBooks, open the invoice.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The Due date reads Oct 19, 2026.

Step 2:

  • The invoice is created.

Step 3:

  • The invoice is no longer on the QB Unexported report.

Step 4:

  • A term named exactly term A now exists, set as a standard term due in 14 days.

Step 5:

  • Its terms read term A and its due date is Oct 19, 2026, the same as in ShopView.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11677 (Story 8, QuickBooks sync - credit terms)

  • S8-R1: “When a record is sent to QuickBooks with a term QuickBooks does not have, ShopView first creates the term in QuickBooks under the same name, then sends the record. This is how the standard terms already work today.”
  • S8-R2: “A "Due Net X days" term is created in QuickBooks as a standard term due in X days.”
  • S8-R5: “Each invoice carries its own term and due date to QuickBooks, as today. A vendor invoice is sent to QuickBooks as a bill with its stored due date (S7-R9) and the vendor's term at the moment it is sent.”
